summary: 1924 Michael Mountain lookout in Seneca State Forest; moved or replaced in 1935 by the Thorny Mountain tower, which still stands and is rented overnight.

facts.design: 45-foot steel forest fire observatory with an observer's house built nearby (January 1925 newspaper)
facts.status_note: Original summit tower relocated or replaced in 1935; sources disagree whether the Thorny Mountain tower is the same structure

staffing.status: observer duties moved to Thorny Mountain

access.note: No source describes access to the original summit. The Thorny Mountain tower in Seneca State Forest is rented overnight by reservation through WV State Parks.

events.note: Tower built on Michael Mountain; register, Forest Lookouts and the state forest history agree on 1924
January 1925 newspaper describes an observer, one ranger and local wardens
Lookout duties moved to Thorny Mountain. Register says the tower was relocated; state forest page says replaced by a newer version
January 1937 report said an observer-quarters tower would go up on Michael Mountain; a November 1937 report says that type was completed on Thorny Mountain
Last staffed year for the Thorny Mountain lookout per Forest Lookouts; state forest page says manned seasonally until the mid-1980s
Lookout transferred to West Virginia State Parks
Thorny Mountain tower reopened for overnight reservations
Registered with Former Fire Lookout Sites on January 26, 2017

corrections.proposed: relocated: original summit site gone; the structure is reported standing as the Thorny Mountain tower
corrections.why: Register says the tower was relocated and continues to stand as Thorny Mountain Fire Tower. The state forest page and Forest Lookouts describe the Thorny tower as a replacement or new site, so whether it is the same structure is disputed.

resolved_conflicts.field: identity of the Thorny Mountain tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says the Michael tower was relocated and still stands at Thorny; the state forest page says it was replaced by a newer version; Forest Lookouts calls Thorny a new site. The story reports all three and does not choose.
A January 1937 report said the observer-quarters type would be erected on Michael Mountain; a November 1937 report says it was completed on Thorny Mountain. The story reports both.
State forest page says manned seasonally until the mid-1980s; Forest Lookouts gives 1988 as the last staffed year.

State forest page says the tower is still available for duty should the need arise, which is undated. Forest Lookouts and The Dyrt describe a 2015 reopening for overnight rental. The story reports the rental.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' understates that a tower stands at Thorny Mountain, but whether it is the 1924 structure is disputed across sources. The state forest page's 'still available for duty' is undated and conflicts with the 2015 rental. The state parks camping page does not itself mention the rental; the rental rests on Forest Lookouts and The Dyrt. No source describes the original summit today.
